title: InfiniBot AIOS · Holo-Canvas
subtitle: The AI Operating System — Voice in, a fleet at work

nodes.body: **InfiniBot is an AI Operating System.** Not a chat box bolted onto a model — a full OS where *agents are first-class processes*: a kernel that routes every call, voice as the primary interface, a fleet of workers, a memory that learns, and a live map of it all.

stats.l: gateway kernel — one RPC surface for everything

nodes.sub: An interactive, free-floating map of the AI Operating System — kernel, interface, processes, memory, scheduler, and the federated machine fleet, all under one voice.
nodes.edition: Gateway · Voice · Fleet · Memory · Workflows · Federation · Activity Mesh

nodes.body: Every real OS has the same parts: a *kernel* that arbitrates, *processes* that do work, a *filesystem* that persists, a *scheduler* that automates, and a *monitor* that shows it all. InfiniBot maps each one onto AI-native primitives — and binds them with **voice** instead of a keyboard.

Everything in InfiniBot speaks through one process: the **gateway**. It is the kernel of the OS. Every UI action, every voice command, every agent tool-call is an RPC into a single registry — there is no second door.

Because the surface is one place, capability is uniform: web, mobile, voice, and a remote satellite all invoke the *same* methods.

The tool surface isn't a static list — it's derived live from `agent.tools.list`. A "missing tool" is never a missing feature; it's a stale build. The kernel is the ground truth, and the MCP bridge re-exports it so external agents get the exact same registry the UI does.
**Why a single kernel matters:** uniform capability is what lets one voice session command web, mobile, and every federated machine identically. One registry, every surface — that is the OS contract.

nodes.caption: K1 · one kernel, many callers — UI, voice, mobile, MCP, satellites all hit one registry

nodes.body:
Most OSes are driven by keyboard and pointer. InfiniBot's primary interface is your **voice**. It is the moat, not a feature: cloud by default, local opt-in, always-on.

You speak a goal; a voice orchestrator understands it, answers instantly, and *delegates the labor* off your critical path. Your eyes never leave the work.

nodes.label: Voice Terminal
nodes.caption: The InfiniBot voice terminal — an always-on holo scene. You speak; the orchestrator listens and dispatches.

nodes.body: The orchestrator prompt has a single source of truth — `voice-orchestrator-prompt.ts` — injected at three spawn points: the web voice stream, the CLI bridge, and mobile. Say *"hey infinibot"* and a wake word flips the surface into live-action mode. The experience is identical wherever you start it.

nodes.body: **Voice is the kernel's shell.** Where a classic OS gives you a terminal, the AIOS gives you a conversation — and the conversation is wired straight into the gateway registry, so anything you can click you can also say.

When the orchestrator delegates, it spawns **processes**: a fleet of coding agents. Four interchangeable backends — `claude`, `codex`, `opencode`, `gemini` — each launched detached, each in its own isolated context. Pick the right brain per job; run as many as the work demands.

nodes.label: Agent Fleet
nodes.caption: The fleet roster — every spawned process, its backend, its task, and its live status in one pane.

nodes.body: A solo chat carries one enormous shared context every turn re-reads. A fleet carries **N small, focused contexts** — one per agent, each holding only what its narrow task needs. The bug-fix agent never reads the migration; each agent's prompt cache stays warm end-to-end.

nodes.body: An OS that forgets is just a shell. InfiniBot persists. **Memory** is a file-per-fact store the gateway searches before any non-trivial task — what worked, what failed, which files matter. **Skills** are versioned playbooks an agent reads on demand. Together they are the AIOS filesystem: the place experience accumulates.

nodes.label: The Grid
nodes.caption: The grid workspace — panels, tools, and live state composed into one OS desktop.

nodes.body: Every agent reads memory at the start and the session-memory hook writes it back at the end — so the next agent inherits what the last one learned. Skills self-heal: when one gives stale instructions, a repair proposal is queued for review. The filesystem gets *better* with use.

nodes.caption: F1 · cost scales with history — memory keeps each context small and topical

nodes.body: **Memory is the compounding layer.** Code captures *structure*; memory captures *judgment* — the non-obvious decisions, the dead ends, the file that isn't where you'd guess. That's why the AIOS reads it before acting.

A fan-out is powerful once. A **workflow** makes it repeatable forever. The workflow engine captures a multi-step process as a named recipe an agent — or you — can run on demand, on a schedule, or in an endless loop. This is the AIOS scheduler: automation that survives the session.

nodes.caption: The workflow library — saved recipes, each tagged; continuous loops sit under Autonomous Control Loops.

nodes.body: **The scheduler feeds the fleet.** A continuous workflow refills the queue on a loop, so the agent processes never go idle — the OS keeps working while you're away from the desk.

A fleet you cannot see is a fleet you cannot trust. The **Activity Mesh** is the OS process monitor — a live, spatial picture of everything running right now. It renders through the live `ActivityMap` engine: every running agent is a body on a world map.

nodes.label: Agency World
nodes.caption: The live agency world — running sub-agents, the spawn feed, credit usage and progression in one glance.

nodes.body: Reach for a tool and the agent physically routes to that **tool sector** and back. Federation links show as **conduits** pulsing as work crosses machines. Idle agents rest in the **concourse** — "busy" and "free" obvious at a glance. Click any agent to drop into its focus modal: live transcript plus a spec-vs-result drift check.

nodes.body:
Parallelism inside one machine eventually hits that machine's limits. **Federation** removes the ceiling — a single voice session commands a fleet that spans *every machine you own*.

It's hub-and-spoke: one **master**, many **satellites**. A satellite never talks directly to another — every cross-node call tunnels through the master via `isLocalNodeId` + `forwardGatewayCall`.

nodes.h3: Each job on the hardware that fits
nodes.body: **Heavy build on the workstation** — the big compile, GPU render, full suite. **Light edits on the laptop** — quick fixes on whatever's nearest. **All from one voice session** — you don't SSH anywhere; the master routes each piece to the right satellite and streams results back to where you're listening.

An OS that only reacts is half an OS. InfiniBot pushes back. The **proactive layer** surfaces media-rich pops on tiered interrupts — CRITICAL center-stage, FYI a corner toast. The **discipline layer** runs your day: COMMIT TO ONE THING up top, DRIFT RADAR watching every active project below.

nodes.label: Morning Board
nodes.caption: The morning board — COMMIT TO ONE THING up top, DRIFT RADAR watching every active project below.

nodes.body: When the drift radar flags an agent wandering off-spec, you don't stop everything — a glance at the focus modal, then a voice course-correction: *"migration agent — drop the schema changes, draft only."* It re-aligns; the rest never break stride. The assistant watches so you can delegate aggressively.

nodes.label: The Desktop
nodes.caption: The dashboard — the AIOS desktop: running work, suggestions, the live world map, all forward-actionable.

nodes.body: InfiniBot is **bring-your-own-key** — you connect your own provider accounts and inference is billed to you, at cost. No token resale, no per-user inference margin. Every isolated context that *saves* tokens saves *your* tokens — and the credits view shows exactly where each one went, across all four backends.

nodes.label: Credit Usage
nodes.caption: Plan-aware tracking across Claude, Codex, OpenCode and Gemini — each backend metered independently, at cost.
C1 · kernel × processes × memory × visibility compound

nodes.body: **The close:** a chat box gives you one model in one window while you wait. InfiniBot AIOS gives you a kernel, a voice shell, a fleet of processes, a memory that learns, a scheduler that never sleeps, and a federated machine fleet — all visible, all yours, all at cost. *That is an AI Operating System.*
